items.t: Children (and, for the suspension, neonates) should only be treated under the guidance of a paediatric specialist.

src.q: Children should only be treated under guidance of a paediatric specialist.
Neonates, children and adolescents should only be treated under guidance of a paediatric specialist.

items.t: Tablets: initially 100 mg daily (single or divided doses), range 25-200 mg daily; maintenance individualised.

src.q: For management of oedema an initial daily dose of 100 mg of spironolactone administered in either single or divided doses is recommended, but may range from 25 mg to 200 mg daily.

items.t: Suspension: usually 100 mg/day, up to 200 mg/day in severe cases; maintenance 75-200 mg/day once oedema controlled.

src.q: Usual dose - 100 mg/day. In difficult or severe cases the dose may be gradually increased up to 200 mg/day. When oedema is controlled, the usual maintenance level is 75 mg/day to 200 mg/day.

items.t: With standard therapy: start 25 mg once daily only if serum potassium is 5.0 mEq/L or less and serum creatinine is 2.5 mg/dL or less (suspension SmPC: 221 micromol/L or less). If tolerated may increase to 50 mg once daily; if 25 mg daily is not tolerated, reduce to 25 mg every other day.

src.q: treatment in conjunction with standard therapy should be initiated at a dose of spironolactone 25 mg once daily if serum potassium is ≤5.0 mEq/L and serum creatinine is ≤2.5 mg/dL.
in patients with a serum potassium ≤ 5.0 mEq/L and serum creatinine ≤ 221 μmol/L

Patients who tolerate 25 mg once daily may have their dose increased to 50 mg once daily as clinically indicated. Patients who do not tolerate 25 mg once daily may have their dose reduced to 25 mg every other day.

items.t: Urinary Na+/K+ ratio above 1.0: 100 mg/day; below 1.0: 200-400 mg/day. Maintenance individualised.
items.tag: Hepatic cirrhosis with ascites and oedema

src.q: If urinary Na+/K+ ratio is greater than 1.0, 100 mg/day. If the ratio is less than 1.0, 200 mg/day to 400 mg/day.

items.t: Initially 100-200 mg/day; up to 400 mg/day in severe cases.

src.q: Initial dose usually 100 mg/day to 200 mg/day. In severe cases the dosage may be gradually increased up to 400 mg/day.

items.t: 100-200 mg/day; only if glucocorticoids alone are not effective enough.

src.q: Usual dose 100 mg/day to 200 mg/day.
Its use is only advised if glucocorticoids by themselves are insufficiently effective.

items.t: Diagnosis: 400 mg daily for 3-4 weeks (long test) or 4 days (short test). Pre-operative: 100-400 mg daily. Long-term if unsuitable for surgery: lowest effective dose.

src.q: Long test: Aldactone is administered at a daily dosage of 400 mg for 3 to 4 weeks.
Short test: Aldactone is administered at a daily dosage of 400 mg for 4 days.
Aldactone may be administered at doses of 100 mg to 400 mg daily in preparation for surgery.

items.t: Suspension only: 50-100 mg/day; in difficult cases increase at 2-weekly intervals up to 200 mg/day. Continue at least 2 weeks before judging response.

src.q: Essential hypertension Usual dose - 50 mg/day to 100 mg/day, which for difficult or severe cases may be gradually increased at 2 weekly intervals up to 200 mg/day.
Treatment should be continued for 2 weeks or longer since an adequate response may not occur before this time.

items.t: Elderly: start at the lowest dose and titrate up as needed.

src.q: It is recommended that treatment is started with the lowest dose and titrated upwards as required to achieve maximum benefit.

items.t: Tablets: initial 1-3 mg/kg daily in divided doses, adjusted to response and tolerance. Specialist guidance only; limited paediatric data.

src.q: Initial daily dosage should provide 1-3 mg of spironolactone per kilogram body weight given in divided doses.

items.t: Suspension - diuresis (heart failure, ascites, oedema, nephrotic syndrome): neonate 1-2 mg/kg daily in 1-2 divided doses; 1 month to 18 years 1-3 mg/kg daily in 1-2 divided doses (maximum 200 mg daily).

src.q: Neonate: 1-2 mg/kg/daily in 1-2 divided doses. Infant or child 1 month to 18 years: 1-3 mg/kg daily in 1-2 divided doses (maximum 200 mg daily).

items.t: Suspension - primary hyperaldosteronism or resistant ascites: neonate up to 7 mg/kg daily; 1 month to 18 years up to 9 mg/kg daily (total maximum 400 mg daily).

src.q: Neonate: up to a maximum of 7 mg/kg daily may be used. Infant or Child 1 month to 18 years: up to a maximum of 9 mg/kg daily (total maximum 400 mg daily) may be used.

items.t: Contraindicated in children with moderate to severe renal impairment (suspension SmPC: GFR 30 to < 60 ml/min and < 30 ml/min). Use with caution in hypertensive children with mild renal insufficiency (hyperkalaemia risk).

src.q: Spironolactone is contraindicated in paediatric patients with moderate to severe renal impairment.
Spironolactone is contraindicated in paediatric patients with moderate (GFR 30 - < 60 ml/min) to severe (GFR < 30 ml/min) renal impairment
Potassium-sparing diuretics should be used with caution in hypertensive paediatric patients with mild renal insufficiency because of the risk of hyperkalaemia.

items.t: Suspension contains sodium benzoate, which may increase neonatal jaundice.

src.q: Increase in bilirubinaemia following its displacement from albumin may increase neonatal jaundice which may develop into kernicterus

items.t: Tablets: acute renal insufficiency, significant renal compromise, anuria; Addison's disease; hyperkalaemia; hypersensitivity; concomitant eplerenone or other potassium-sparing diuretics.

src.q: acute renal insufficiency, significant renal compromise, anuria Addison's disease hyperkalaemia hypersensitivity to spironolactone or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1 concomitant use of eplerenone or other potassium sparing diuretics.

items.t: Suspension: hypersensitivity; acute renal insufficiency, severe renal impairment (GFR < 30 ml/min), anuria; Addison's disease; hyperkalaemia (> 5.5 mEq/L); concomitant eplerenone.

src.q: Acute renal insufficiency, severe renal impairment (GFR < 30 ml/min), anuria - Addison's disease - Hyperkalaemia (> 5.5 mEq/L) - Concomitant use of eplerenone.

items.t: Do not give with other potassium-conserving diuretics; do not give potassium supplements routinely.

src.q: Aldactone should not be administered concurrently with other potassium conserving diuretics and potassium supplements should not be given routinely with Aldactone as hyperkalaemia may be induced.

items.t: Hyperkalaemia, which can cause fatal arrhythmias, may occur with renal impairment or high potassium intake. Stop spironolactone if hyperkalaemia develops.

src.q: Hyperkalaemia may occur in patients with impaired renal function or excessive potassium intake and can cause cardiac irregularities which may be fatal.
Should hyperkalaemia develop Aldactone should be discontinued

items.t: Severe heart failure: monitor and manage potassium; avoid other potassium-sparing diuretics; avoid oral potassium supplements if potassium is above 3.5 mEq/L. Stop or interrupt if potassium > 5 mEq/L or creatinine > 4 mg/dL (suspension SmPC: > 353 micromol/L).

src.q: It is critical to monitor and manage serum potassium in patients with severe heart failure receiving spironolactone. Avoid using other potassium-sparing diuretics. Avoid using oral potassium supplements in patients with serum potassium >3.5 mEq/L.
Discontinue or interrupt treatment for serum potassium >5 mEq/L or for serum creatinine >4 mg/dL
Discontinue or interrupt treatment for serum potassium > 5 mEq/L or for serum creatinine > 353 μmol/L

items.t: Monitor fluid and electrolytes regularly, especially in the elderly and in significant renal or hepatic impairment.

src.q: Fluid and electrolyte status should be regularly monitored particularly in the elderly, in those with significant renal and hepatic impairment.

items.t: Decompensated hepatic cirrhosis: reversible hyperchloraemic metabolic acidosis (usually with hyperkalaemia) reported, even with normal renal function.

src.q: Reversible hyperchloraemic metabolic acidosis, usually in association with hyperkalaemia has been reported to occur in some patients with decompensated hepatic cirrhosis, even in the presence of normal renal function.

items.t: Suspension SmPC: use with particular caution in the elderly, possible urinary tract obstruction, or unstable electrolyte balance; dilutional hyponatraemia may occur with other diuretics.

src.q: The preparation should only be used with particular caution in elderly patients or those with potential obstruction of the urinary tract, or with disorders rendering their electrolyte balance precarious.
Dilution hyponatraemia may occur in combination with other diuretics

items.t: Suspension contains 400 mg sucrose per ml: patients with hereditary fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take it; take into account in diabetes; may harm teeth.

src.q: As this medicinal product contains 400 mg sucrose per ml, this has to be taken into consideration in terms of daily intake. This should be taken into account in patients with diabetes mellitus.
Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take this medicine.

items.t: Regional or general anaesthesia: take care (reduced vascular response to noradrenaline).

src.q: Caution should be exercised in the management of patients subjected to regional or general anaesthesia while they are being treated with Aldactone.

items.t: Medicines that raise potassium (other potassium-sparing diuretics, ACE inhibitors, NSAIDs, ARBs, aldosterone blockers, heparins, potassium supplements, potassium-rich diet or salt substitutes): may cause severe hyperkalaemia. Co-trimoxazole: clinically relevant hyperkalaemia.

src.q: Concomitant use of Aldactone with other potassium-sparing diuretics, angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, angiotensin II antagonists, aldosterone blockers, heparin, low molecular weight heparin
may lead to severe hyperkalaemia.
concomitant use of trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole (co-trimoxazole) with spironolactone may result in clinically relevant hyperkalaemia.

items.t: ACE inhibitors: SmPC - should not routinely be used together, particularly in marked renal impairment. MHRA (heart failure) - the combination raises the risk of severe hyperkalaemia, particularly in marked renal impairment, and should be used with caution: use the lowest effective doses, monitor potassium and renal function regularly, and interrupt or stop if hyperkalaemia occurs.

src.q: Since ACE inhibitors decrease aldosterone production they should not routinely be used with Aldactone, particularly in patients with marked renal impairment.
concomitant use of spironolactone with ACEi or ARB increases the risk of severe hyperkalaemia, particularly in patients with marked renal impairment, and should be used with caution

use the lowest effective doses of spironolactone and ACEi or ARB if coadministration is considered essential regularly monitor serum potassium levels and renal function interrupt or discontinue treatment in the event of hyperkalaemia

items.t: MHRA: the triple combination of an ACE inhibitor, an ARB and a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (or other potassium-sparing diuretic) is not recommended.

src.q: The triple combination of an ACE-inhibitor, ARB, and a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist or other potassium-sparing diuretic is not recommended.

items.t: NSAIDs (e.g. aspirin, indometacin, mefenamic acid): reduce the diuretic effect, and add to hyperkalaemia risk.

src.q: have been shown to attenuate the diuretic effect of spironolactone.

items.t: Other antihypertensives (and other diuretics): effect potentiated; their dose may need reducing (suspension SmPC: by about 50%) and then adjusting.

src.q: Potentiation of the effect of antihypertensive drugs occurs and their dosage may need to be reduced when Aldactone is added to the treatment regime and then adjusted as necessary.
their dose may need to be reduced by about 50% when spironolactone is added to the treatment regime

items.t: Digoxin: spironolactone may raise digoxin levels and interfere with digoxin assays; monitor digoxin response by other means unless the assay is unaffected.

src.q: In patients receiving digoxin and spironolactone the digoxin response should be monitored by means other than serum digoxin concentrations, unless the digoxin assay used has been proven not to be affected by spironolactone therapy.

items.t: Lithium: risk of lithium toxicity; monitor lithium levels. Abiraterone: not recommended (PSA may rise). Mitotane: do not use together. Carbenoxolone: avoid.

src.q: Monitor lithium levels periodically when spironolactone is coadministered.
Use with abiraterone is not recommended.
should not be used concomitantly with mitotane

items.t: SmPC (tablets): limited data; anti-androgenic reproductive toxicity in animals. Diuretics may reduce placental perfusion and are not recommended for standard treatment of hypertension and oedema in pregnancy. Should not be used unless the potential benefit justifies the risk.

src.q: Diuretics can lead to reduced perfusion of the placenta and thus to impairment of intrauterine growth and are therefore not recommended for the standard therapy for hypertension and oedema during pregnancy.
Spironolactone should not be used during pregnancy, unless the potential benefit justifies the potential risk.

items.t: BUMPS (diuretics): rarely needed in pregnancy; may reduce placental blood flow (extra growth scans). Spironolactone may lower fetal testosterone, with concern about male genital development (animal data; one human case report, several normal). Recommended only if benefit outweighs risk.

src.q: Use of spironolactone specifically can potentially reduce levels of the male hormone testosterone in the baby.
Use of a diuretic in pregnancy will only be recommended if the benefits of treating a potentially serious condition outweigh the possible risks.
